/-!
# McMullen problem

Larman [La72], crediting a private communication of Peter McMullen, posed the following problem:
determine the largest number $\nu(d)$ such that any $\nu(d)$ points in general position in affine
$d$-space $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be mapped into convex position (so that they form the vertices of a
convex polytope) by a permissible projective transformation.

Here a finite point set is in *general position* if no $d + 1$ of its points lie on a common
hyperplane, a projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is the map induced on the affine chart
$\{(x, 1)\}$ by an invertible linear map of $\mathbb{R}^{d + 1}$ (homogeneous coordinates), and
such a transformation is *permissible* for a point set if it sends none of the points to the
hyperplane at infinity.

Larman proved $2d + 1 \le \nu(d) \le (d + 1)^2$, and the conjectured answer is $\nu(d) = 2d + 1$.
This is known for $d = 2, 3, 4$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, McMullen problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McMullen_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [La72] Larman, D. G., *On sets projectively equivalent to the vertices of a convex polytope*,
  Bull. London Math. Soc. 4 (1972), 6–12.
-/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def projectiveMap (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (x : ℝ^d) :
    ℝ^d :=
  (g (x, 1)).2⁻¹ • (g (x, 1)).1
blocks.docstring:
The projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ induced by a linear automorphism `g` of the
homogeneous coordinate space $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d + 1}$, evaluated
at `x`: lift `x` to `(x, 1)`, apply `g`, and dehomogenise. In block form
$g = \begin{pmatrix} A & b \\ c^{\mathsf T} & \delta \end{pmatrix}$ this is
$x \mapsto (Ax + b) / (\langle c, x \rangle + \delta)$. The value is only meaningful when the last
homogeneous coordinate `(g (x, 1)).2` is nonzero, i.e. when `x` is not sent to the hyperplane at
infinity; see `McMullenProblem.IsPermissible`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `Projectivization` with the `MulAction` of the general linear group (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projectivization/Action.lean); `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup`.
justification.name: McMullenProblem.projectiveMap
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a projective transformation acting on the affine chart ℝ^d ⊂ ℝP^d (fractional-linear map with dehomogenisation). `Projectivization` and its GL-action exist but provide no affine chart/dehomogenisation, so a direct definition via homogeneous coordinates ℝ^d × ℝ is clearer.

blocks.text:

noncomputable def projectiveMap (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (x : ℝ^d) :
    ℝ^d :=

blocks.code:
def IsPermissible (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ S, (g (x, 1)).2 ≠ 0
blocks.docstring:
The projective transformation induced by `g` is *permissible* for the finite point set `S` if it
sends no point of `S` to the hyperplane at infinity, i.e. it is defined at every point of `S`.

justification.name: McMullenProblem.IsPermissible
justification.why_needed: Expresses that the projective transformation sends no point of the given set to the hyperplane at infinity (last homogeneous coordinate nonzero); no Mathlib counterpart.

blocks.name: IsPermissible
blocks.text:
/--
The projective transformation induced by `g` is *permissible* for the finite point set `S` if it
sends no point of `S` to the hyperplane at infinity, i.e. it is defined at every point of `S`.
-/
def IsPermissible (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ S, (g (x, 1)).2 ≠ 0

blocks.code:
def InGeneralPosition (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ T ⊆ S, T.card ≤ d + 1 → AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : T → ℝ^d)
blocks.docstring:
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in *general position* if any at most `d + 1` of
its points are affinely independent. For sets with at least `d + 1` points this says exactly that
no `d + 1` of the points lie on a common hyperplane.

justification.name: McMullenProblem.InGeneralPosition
justification.why_needed: General position in ℝ^d (any ≤ d+1 points affinely independent) is not in Mathlib; the repo's `InGeneralPosition` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean is planar and includes a no-four-concyclic condition, which is the wrong notion here.

blocks.name: InGeneralPosition
blocks.text:
/--
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in *general position* if any at most `d + 1` of
its points are affinely independent. For sets with at least `d + 1` points this says exactly that
no `d + 1` of the points lie on a common hyperplane.
-/
def InGeneralPosition (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ T ⊆ S, T.card ≤ d + 1 → AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : T → ℝ^d)

blocks.docstring:
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ *can be projectively transformed into convex
position* if some projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is permissible for `S` maps
the points of `S` into convex position, i.e. every image point is a vertex of the convex hull of
the image points (`ConvexIndependent`).
blocks.name: IsProjectivelyConvexifiable
blocks.text:
/--
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ *can be projectively transformed into convex
position* if some projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is permissible for `S` maps
the points of `S` into convex position, i.e. every image point is a vertex of the convex hull of
the image points (`ConvexIndependent`).
-/
def IsProjectivelyConvexifiable (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ),
    IsPermissible g S ∧ ConvexIndependent ℝ fun x : S => projectiveMap g x

blocks.code:
def CanBeMadeConvex (d n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset (ℝ^d), S.card = n → InGeneralPosition S → IsProjectivelyConvexifiable S
blocks.docstring:
`CanBeMadeConvex d n` says that every set of `n` points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$
can be mapped into convex position by a permissible projective transformation. The number
$\nu(d)$ of the McMullen problem is the largest `n` with this property.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None; built from `ConvexIndependent` and the definitions above.
justification.name: McMullenProblem.CanBeMadeConvex
justification.why_needed: The predicate 'every n points in general position in ℝ^d can be mapped into convex position by a permissible projective transformation', whose maximal n defines ν(d).

blocks.name: CanBeMadeConvex
blocks.text:
/--
`CanBeMadeConvex d n` says that every set of `n` points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$
can be mapped into convex position by a permissible projective transformation. The number
$\nu(d)$ of the McMullen problem is the largest `n` with this property.
-/
def CanBeMadeConvex (d n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset (ℝ^d), S.card = n → InGeneralPosition S → IsProjectivelyConvexifiable S

@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsProjectivelyConvexifiable.of_convexIndependent {S : Finset (ℝ^d)}
    (hS : ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : S → ℝ^d)) : IsProjectivelyConvexifiable S :=
  ⟨LinearEquiv.refl ℝ _, isPermissible_refl S, by simpa [projectiveMap_refl] using hS⟩

theorem canBeMadeConvex_zero (d : ℕ) : CanBeMadeConvex d 0 := by
  intro S hS _
  rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at hS
  subst hS
  exact .of_convexIndependent (Subsingleton.convexIndependent _)

  subst hS

theorem mcmullen_problem (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    IsGreatest {n | CanBeMadeConvex d n} (2 * d + 1) := by

blocks.docstring:
**The McMullen problem.** Let $\nu(d)$ be the largest number such that any $\nu(d)$ points in
general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (no $d + 1$ of them on a common hyperplane) can be mapped into
convex position (so that they form the vertices of a convex polytope) by a permissible projective
transformation (one sending none of the points to the hyperplane at infinity). The conjecture is
that $\nu(d) = 2d + 1$ for every $d \geq 2$, i.e. $2d + 1$ is the largest `n` such that
`CanBeMadeConvex d n` holds.

The restriction $d \geq 2$ is needed: on the line at most two points can be in convex position,
so $\nu(1) = 2$.

claims.decomposer_note: The list entry only names the problem; per the article it asks to determine the largest ν(d) such that every ν(d) points in general position in ℝ^d admit a permissible projective transformation (one not sending any of the points to the hyperplane at infinity) taking them into convex position (all points vertices of their convex hull, i.e. ConvexIndependent), and the article asserts the candidate answer ν(d) = 2d+1, so the Prop is 'ν(d) = 2d+1' (for d ≥ 2; for d = 1 one has ν(1) = 2, so the range of d must be restricted), where ν(d) is well defined as a maximum since the property is downward-closed in the number of points and Larman's bounds 2d+1 ≤ ν(d) ≤ (d+1)^2 make it finite; the Gale-transform (μ), hull-partition (λ) and projective-dual formulations are equivalent restatements, and the known bounds and the proven cases d = 2,3,4 are results, not further questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and encode the same (correct) reading of Larman's problem: points of ℝ^d, general position = every ≤ d+1 subfamily affinely independent (equivalent to 'no d+1 on a hyperplane' for the relevant sizes and downward-closed), projective transformation = linear automorphism of the homogeneous space ℝ^{d+1} acting on the chart (x,1), permissibility = last homogeneous coordinate nonzero at each given point (the loose Larman sense — the strict hull-avoiding sense would force ν(d)=d+1, contradicting Larman's 2d+1 lower bound), convex position = Mathlib `ConvexIndependent` of the image family (injectivity is automatic for a permissible projective map), and the Prop ν(d)=2d+1 for d ≥ 2. I took c07's `IsGreatest {n | ...} (2d+1)` formulation because it states 'largest n such that ...' directly without relying on the ℕ `sSup` junk value (equivalent to the sSup versions of c01/c03/c04/c05/c08 since 2d+1 ≠ 0, but more transparent), combined with c04's cleaner named predicates (`projectiveMap`, `IsPermissible`, `InGeneralPosition`, `IsProjectivelyConvexifiable`, `CanBeMadeConvex`) and proven API/test lemmas (identity is permissible and acts as identity, empty set case). Points live in `ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` following repo idiom (Kakeya.lean).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# McMullen problem

Larman [La72], crediting a private communication of Peter McMullen, posed the following problem:
determine the largest number $\nu(d)$ such that any $\nu(d)$ points in general position in affine
$d$-space $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be mapped into convex position (so that they form the vertices of a
convex polytope) by a permissible projective transformation.

Here a finite point set is in *general position* if no $d + 1$ of its points lie on a common
hyperplane, a projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is the map induced on the affine chart
$\{(x, 1)\}$ by an invertible linear map of $\mathbb{R}^{d + 1}$ (homogeneous coordinates), and
such a transformation is *permissible* for a point set if it sends none of the points to the
hyperplane at infinity.

Larman proved $2d + 1 \le \nu(d) \le (d + 1)^2$, and the conjectured answer is $\nu(d) = 2d + 1$.
This is known for $d = 2, 3, 4$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, McMullen problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McMullen_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [La72] Larman, D. G., *On sets projectively equivalent to the vertices of a convex polytope*,
  Bull. London Math. Soc. 4 (1972), 6–12.
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace McMullenProblem

variable {d : ℕ}

/--
The projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ induced by a linear automorphism `g` of the
homogeneous coordinate space $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} \cong \mathbb{R}^{d + 1}$, evaluated
at `x`: lift `x` to `(x, 1)`, apply `g`, and dehomogenise. In block form
$g = \begin{pmatrix} A & b \\ c^{\mathsf T} & \delta \end{pmatrix}$ this is
$x \mapsto (Ax + b) / (\langle c, x \rangle + \delta)$. The value is only meaningful when the last
homogeneous coordinate `(g (x, 1)).2` is nonzero, i.e. when `x` is not sent to the hyperplane at
infinity; see `McMullenProblem.IsPermissible`.
-/
noncomputable def projectiveMap (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (x : ℝ^d) :
    ℝ^d :=
  (g (x, 1)).2⁻¹ • (g (x, 1)).1

/--
The projective transformation induced by `g` is *permissible* for the finite point set `S` if it
sends no point of `S` to the hyperplane at infinity, i.e. it is defined at every point of `S`.
-/
def IsPermissible (g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)) (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x ∈ S, (g (x, 1)).2 ≠ 0

/--
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in *general position* if any at most `d + 1` of
its points are affinely independent. For sets with at least `d + 1` points this says exactly that
no `d + 1` of the points lie on a common hyperplane.
-/
def InGeneralPosition (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∀ T ⊆ S, T.card ≤ d + 1 → AffineIndependent ℝ ((↑) : T → ℝ^d)

/--
A finite set `S` of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ *can be projectively transformed into convex
position* if some projective transformation of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that is permissible for `S` maps
the points of `S` into convex position, i.e. every image point is a vertex of the convex hull of
the image points (`ConvexIndependent`).
-/
def IsProjectivelyConvexifiable (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ),
    IsPermissible g S ∧ ConvexIndependent ℝ fun x : S => projectiveMap g x

/--
`CanBeMadeConvex d n` says that every set of `n` points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$
can be mapped into convex position by a permissible projective transformation. The number
$\nu(d)$ of the McMullen problem is the largest `n` with this property.
-/
def CanBeMadeConvex (d n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset (ℝ^d), S.card = n → InGeneralPosition S → IsProjectivelyConvexifiable S

/-- The identity of $\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}$ induces the identity transformation. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem projectiveMap_refl (x : ℝ^d) : projectiveMap (LinearEquiv.refl ℝ _) x = x := by
  simp [projectiveMap]

/-- The identity transformation is permissible for every finite point set. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem isPermissible_refl (S : Finset (ℝ^d)) : IsPermissible (LinearEquiv.refl ℝ _) S :=
  fun _ _ => one_ne_zero

/-- A set that is already in convex position can be projectively transformed into convex
position, via the identity. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem IsProjectivelyConvexifiable.of_convexIndependent {S : Finset (ℝ^d)}
    (hS : ConvexIndependent ℝ ((↑) : S → ℝ^d)) : IsProjectivelyConvexifiable S :=
  ⟨LinearEquiv.refl ℝ _, isPermissible_refl S, by simpa [projectiveMap_refl] using hS⟩

/-- The empty set can be projectively transformed into convex position. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem canBeMadeConvex_zero (d : ℕ) : CanBeMadeConvex d 0 := by
  intro S hS _
  rw [Finset.card_eq_zero] at hS
  subst hS
  exact .of_convexIndependent (Subsingleton.convexIndependent _)

/--
**The McMullen problem.** Let $\nu(d)$ be the largest number such that any $\nu(d)$ points in
general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$ (no $d + 1$ of them on a common hyperplane) can be mapped into
convex position (so that they form the vertices of a convex polytope) by a permissible projective
transformation (one sending none of the points to the hyperplane at infinity). The conjecture is
that $\nu(d) = 2d + 1$ for every $d \geq 2$, i.e. $2d + 1$ is the largest `n` such that
`CanBeMadeConvex d n` holds.

The restriction $d \geq 2$ is needed: on the line at most two points can be in convex position,
so $\nu(1) = 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 52]
theorem mcmullen_problem (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d) :
    IsGreatest {n | CanBeMadeConvex d n} (2 * d + 1) := by
  sorry

end McMullenProblem

items: Projective transformations of ℝ^d are parametrised by linear automorphisms `T : (ℝ^d × ℝ) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (ℝ^d × ℝ)` of homogeneous coordinates, with x ∈ ℝ^d embedded as (x, 1) and image `(T (x,1)).2⁻¹ • (T (x,1)).1`. Every element of PGL(d+1, ℝ) arises this way (overparametrisation by scalars is harmless).

'Permissible' is taken in the loose sense of the decomposition notes: no point of the set is sent to the hyperplane at infinity, i.e. `(T (x,1)).2 ≠ 0` for all x ∈ S. The stricter Grünbaum notion (hyperplane at infinity missing the whole convex hull) would make the problem trivial (such maps preserve convex position, forcing ν(d) = d+1), so the loose notion is the only faithful reading; it also matches the Wikipedia hull-partition reformulation.

'General position' in ℝ^d is formalised as: every subset of at most d+1 points is affinely independent (equivalently, no d+1 points lie on a common hyperplane). Using '≤ d+1' rather than '= d+1' avoids a vacuous condition for small sets; for the sizes relevant to the conjecture (≥ 2d+1) the two agree.

'Convex position' is `ConvexIndependent ℝ (fun x : S => projectiveMap T x)` on the family indexed by S. Since a permissible projective transformation is injective on S, this coincides with 'the image set is in convex position' and forces all |S| image points to be vertices of their convex hull.

'ν(d) = 2d+1' is rendered as `IsGreatest (cardSet d) (2 * d + 1)`, i.e. 2d+1 is the largest n such that every n points in general position can be transformed into convex position. This is literally the definition of ν(d) as a maximum and avoids reliance on `sSup` junk values; it is equivalent to `sSup (cardSet d) = 2d+1` given Larman's finiteness bound and downward closure of `cardSet d`.
The range is restricted to d ≥ 2 as instructed by the notes (ν(1) = 2, since at most two points of ℝ^1 can be in convex position); this is explained in the theorem docstring.
Points live in `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` (repo notation `ℝ^d`); only the affine/convex structure is used.

Known results (Larman's bounds, Las Vergnas / Ramírez Alfonsín upper bounds, proven cases d = 2,3,4) are not stated, per the decomposition notes. Only small test/API lemmas for the bespoke definitions were added (identity transformation; convex-independent sets satisfy the predicate).

reviewer_notes: The list entry only names the problem; the formalized Prop follows the decomposition table and the Wikipedia article: for d ≥ 2, 2d+1 is the largest n such that every n-point set in general position in ℝ^d admits a permissible projective transformation into convex position. Boundary checks: d ≥ 2 is required (ν(1)=2 since three collinear points are never in convex position under any permissible projective map; d=0 degenerate); `CanBeMadeConvex d 0` holds (proved as a test), so the set is nonempty; the set is downward closed and bounded by Larman's (d+1)^2, so IsGreatest agrees with the informal maximum. Candidates c03, c04 and c08 additionally shipped sorry'd `research solved` variants (Larman/Las Vergnas/Ramírez Alfonsín bounds, d=2,3,4 cases); these are outside the single slot and their exact ranges of d were not verified against the primary sources, so they were deliberately not included. Only proven test/API lemmas for the bespoke definitions were added, per the repository's 'add basic API tests' rule. No candidate objected to the decomposition; none omitted the slot. One reference line (a Wikipedia URL) exceeds 100 characters; the repository has precedent for long URL lines (e.g. ABC.lean).
statement: The McMullen problem on projectively transforming sets of points into convex position
